# Story 21 — Live Chat Communication Channel

## Prerequisites

- Story 07 completed: Customer identify/create flow available via `backend/src/CustomerSupportCrm.Api/Customers/CustomersService.cs`.
- Story 08 completed: `CustomerInteraction` model/service exists at `backend/src/CustomerSupportCrm.Api/Customers/Interactions/` and `backend/src/CustomerSupportCrm.Domain/Customers/CustomerInteraction.cs`.
- Story 11 completed: Ticket Creation flow available via `backend/src/CustomerSupportCrm.Api/Tickets/Tickets/TicketsService.cs`.
- Story 12 completed: Manual ticket assignment via existing `TicketsService`/`TicketsController` (assign endpoint).
- Story 14 completed: `TicketHistoryService` exists at `backend/src/CustomerSupportCrm.Api/Tickets/History/TicketHistoryService.cs`. Must **not** duplicate or take over its responsibility.
- Story 17 completed: Quick Replies at `backend/src/CustomerSupportCrm.Api/QuickReplies/` and `frontend/src/features/quick-replies/`. Must be reused as-is.
- Coordination with owner of **Story 23 (Automatic Ticket Assignment)**: this story introduces an integration seam `IChatAssignmentDispatcher` that Story 23 will implement. Story 21 must ship a **manual/waiting-only default implementation** and must **not** add any auto-selection logic.
- **SignalR not currently used in the repo** (verified: no `Hub` classes and no `SignalR` references under `backend/src/CustomerSupportCrm.Api/`). This story introduces the first SignalR hub and Program.cs registrations.

---

## Story Goal

Add a Live Chat communication channel that lets a Customer start a real-time conversation with the CRM and lets a human Agent reply through a persisted, ticket-linked chat conversation. Concretely:

1. A public customer-facing endpoint that starts a chat session, identifying/creating a Customer via existing services and creating/linking a Ticket via existing `TicketsService`.
2. A new `LiveChatConversation` + `LiveChatMessage` domain aggregate persisted in EF Core, linked to `Customer` and `Ticket`.
3. A SignalR hub that streams messages between Customer and Agent, plus REST endpoints so history survives reconnect/refresh.
4. Reuse of the existing `CustomerInteraction` service to record the chat as a customer interaction.
5. An assignment integration seam (`IChatAssignmentDispatcher`) with a default no-auto-select implementation that leaves conversations in `Waiting` state until a manual assign happens through existing Story 12 flow.
6. Reuse of the existing Quick Replies API and picker in the Agent UI — selecting a Quick Reply **populates the input only**; Send must be explicit.

**Out of scope (do not implement):** any automatic agent selection algorithm, AI/chatbot replies, Story 12 manual assign changes, Story 14 TicketHistory rework, Story 17 Quick Reply CRUD changes.

## Product rules (from story)

**Current behaviour**
- No Live Chat channel exists.
- No SignalR hub exists.
- Quick Replies are only used from ticket/customer contexts.

**New behaviour**
- New `LiveChatConversation` aggregate with lifecycle `Waiting → Active → Closed` (reopen allowed only via explicit action).
- Assignment: Live Chat **never** picks an Agent. On creation, conversation is `Waiting`. Manual assignment (Story 12) transitions it to `Active`. Story 23 will later plug into `IChatAssignmentDispatcher.RequestAssignmentAsync` — a no-op default in this story.
- Quick Reply selection **inserts text** into the composer input; **Send is a separate explicit action**. Quick Reply selection creates **no** database rows, no message, no interaction, no history entry.
- Only the actual sent `LiveChatMessage` produces persistence, SignalR broadcast, `CustomerInteraction`, and TicketHistory entry (via `TicketHistoryService`).

## Backend Tasks

### 1 — Domain entities

**Create file:** `backend/src/CustomerSupportCrm.Domain/LiveChat/LiveChatConversation.cs`

```csharp
namespace CustomerSupportCrm.Domain.LiveChat;

public enum LiveChatConversationStatus
{
    Waiting = 0,
    Active = 1,
    Closed = 2,
}

public class LiveChatConversation
{
    public Guid Id { get; set; }
    public Guid CustomerId { get; set; }
    public Guid TicketId { get; set; }
    public Guid? AssignedUserId { get; set; }              // set by Story 12 manual assign or Story 23 later
    public LiveChatConversationStatus Status { get; set; } = LiveChatConversationStatus.Waiting;
    public DateTimeOffset CreatedAtUtc { get; set; }
    public DateTimeOffset? ClosedAtUtc { get; set; }
    public string? VisitorDisplayName { get; set; }
    public string? VisitorSessionToken { get; set; }       // opaque token returned to unauthenticated customer
    public List<LiveChatMessage> Messages { get; set; } = new();
}
```

**Create file:** `backend/src/CustomerSupportCrm.Domain/LiveChat/LiveChatMessage.cs`

```csharp
namespace CustomerSupportCrm.Domain.LiveChat;

public enum LiveChatSender { Customer = 0, Agent = 1, System = 2 }

public class LiveChatMessage
{
    public Guid Id { get; set; }
    public Guid ConversationId { get; set; }
    public LiveChatConversation Conversation { get; set; } = default!;
    public LiveChatSender Sender { get; set; }
    public Guid? SenderUserId { get; set; }                // null when Sender == Customer
    public string Body { get; set; } = string.Empty;
    public DateTimeOffset SentAtUtc { get; set; }
    public long Sequence { get; set; }                     // monotonic per conversation for ordering
}
```

### 5 — Live Chat service

**Create files:**
- `backend/src/CustomerSupportCrm.Api/LiveChat/ILiveChatService.cs`
- `backend/src/CustomerSupportCrm.Api/LiveChat/LiveChatService.cs`
- `backend/src/CustomerSupportCrm.Api/LiveChat/LiveChatDtos.cs`

`ILiveChatService` methods:

```csharp
Task<StartChatResult> StartAsync(StartChatRequest req, CancellationToken ct);   // customer-facing
Task<ChatConversationDto> GetAsync(Guid conversationId, CancellationToken ct);
Task<IReadOnlyList<ChatMessageDto>> GetMessagesAsync(Guid conversationId, long? afterSequence, CancellationToken ct);
Task<ChatMessageDto> AppendCustomerMessageAsync(Guid conversationId, string sessionToken, string body, CancellationToken ct);
Task<ChatMessageDto> AppendAgentMessageAsync(Guid conversationId, Guid agentUserId, string body, CancellationToken ct);
Task<ChatConversationDto> CloseAsync(Guid conversationId, Guid actingUserId, CancellationToken ct);
Task<ChatConversationDto> ReopenAsync(Guid conversationId, Guid actingUserId, CancellationToken ct);
Task<IReadOnlyList<ChatConversationDto>> ListForAgentAsync(Guid agentUserId, ChatFilter filter, CancellationToken ct);
```

`StartChatRequest` fields: `VisitorDisplayName?`, `Email?`, `Phone?`, `Subject?`, `FirstMessage`, optional `ExistingTicketId?`.

`StartAsync` flow (in order, single EF `SaveChangesAsync` where possible):

1. Call `ICustomersService` to find-or-create the customer from email/phone/name using the existing identify-or-create method. **Do not** duplicate customer creation logic.
2. If `ExistingTicketId` supplied and the caller has permission, load it; otherwise call `ITicketsService.CreateAsync` with channel/source = `"LiveChat"`, subject from request, description = first message text. **Do not** duplicate ticket creation logic.
3. Create `LiveChatConversation` (`Waiting`, generate `VisitorSessionToken` = `Guid.NewGuid().ToString("N")`).
4. Persist first `LiveChatMessage` (sender = `Customer`, `Sequence = 1`).
5. Call `ICustomerInteractionsService` to record the interaction with channel `"LiveChat"`, linked to `CustomerId` and `TicketId`. **Reuse the existing service.**
6. Call `ITicketHistoryService` to record `LiveChatOpened` event. TicketHistory ownership stays with Story 14; Live Chat only calls the existing API.
7. Call `IChatAssignmentDispatcher.RequestAssignmentAsync`. If it returns a user id, set `AssignedUserId` and `Status = Active`; else remain `Waiting`.
8. Return `StartChatResult { ConversationId, SessionToken, TicketId, CustomerId, Status }`.

`AppendAgentMessageAsync`:
- Verify caller is the assigned agent (or has override permission).
- Append `LiveChatMessage` with monotonic `Sequence` (max+1 per conversation, computed inside a transaction/serialisable read).
- Call `ICustomerInteractionsService` **only for the sent message** (per intake rule 37/38: only sent messages create interaction records — sending a Quick Reply preview does not).
- Broadcast via SignalR hub (see task 7).
- Return persisted DTO.

`AppendCustomerMessageAsync`: identical except no assignment check; validate `VisitorSessionToken` matches conversation.

`CloseAsync` / `ReopenAsync`: transition status, timestamp `ClosedAtUtc`, emit TicketHistory event via existing service.

### 6 — REST controller

**Create file:** `backend/src/CustomerSupportCrm.Api/LiveChat/LiveChatController.cs`

Routes and auth:

- `POST /api/live-chat/sessions` — **`[AllowAnonymous]`** — customer starts a chat. Returns `StartChatResult` including `SessionToken` used by the widget.
- `POST /api/live-chat/sessions/{id}/messages/customer` — **`[AllowAnonymous]`** — body carries session token. Appends a customer message.
- `GET /api/live-chat/sessions/{id}/messages?afterSequence=` — session-token protected (customer) or `[HasPermission("LiveChat.View")]` (agent). Used for reconnect/refresh replay.
- `GET /api/live-chat/agent/conversations?status=` — `[HasPermission("LiveChat.View")]` — list for the agent.
- `GET /api/live-chat/agent/conversations/{id}` — `[HasPermission("LiveChat.View")]`.
- `POST /api/live-chat/agent/conversations/{id}/messages` — `[HasPermission("LiveChat.Send")]` — appends agent message.
- `POST /api/live-chat/agent/conversations/{id}/close` — `[HasPermission("LiveChat.Close")]`.
- `POST /api/live-chat/agent/conversations/{id}/reopen` — `[HasPermission("LiveChat.Reopen")]`.

Follow the controller shape used in `backend/src/CustomerSupportCrm.Api/Tickets/Collaboration/TicketCollaborationCommentsController.cs`.

Behaviour:

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Empty first message on `StartAsync`** — 400; validate min length 1 char in `LiveChatService.StartAsync`.
- **Unicode / emoji in message body** — persist as `nvarchar(max)`; no truncation; SignalR JSON payload handles UTF-8 by default.
- **Extremely long messages** — enforce a server-side max (e.g. 4000 chars) in `LiveChatService`; return 400 with `MessageTooLong`.
- **Concurrent sends to the same conversation** — `Sequence` computed as `MAX(Sequence)+1` inside a transaction with `IsolationLevel.Serializable`, or use a `RowVersion` retry loop. Prevents duplicate sequence numbers.
- **Customer refresh / SignalR disconnect** — widget re-reads session from `sessionStorage`, calls `GET messages?afterSequence=<last>` to reconcile before subscribing. Enforced in `liveChatHub.ts` reconnect handler and `LiveChatWidget.tsx` mount.
- **Session token replay / theft** — token is opaque and per-conversation; do not accept a token for a different conversation id. Enforced in `AppendCustomerMessageAsync`.
- **Agent tries to send while unassigned** — 403; enforced in `AppendAgentMessageAsync`.
- **Agent tries to send to a Closed conversation** — 409 `ConversationClosed`; enforced in service.
- **Reopen without permission** — 403 via `LiveChat.Reopen`.
- **No agent available** — conversation remains `Waiting` indefinitely. Manual assignment via existing Story 12 flow flips status to `Active`. **No timeout-based auto-close in this story.**
- **Story 23 not yet installed** — `ManualOnlyChatAssignmentDispatcher` returns `null`, keeping the conversation `Waiting`. Correct by design.
- **Quick Reply selection race** — picker only mutates local textarea state. No API call. No message row. Verified in tests.
- **Duplicate customer identification** — rely on `ICustomersService` existing dedup; do not add a second dedup path.
- **Anonymous customer with no email or phone** — allowed; `Customer` created with generated placeholder per existing Story 07 rules. Do not add Live Chat-specific customer fields.
- **Ticket already Closed** when `ExistingTicketId` is provided — 409; require caller to create a new ticket.

## Migration / Rollback

- Migration file: `AddLiveChat` under `backend/src/CustomerSupportCrm.Infrastructure/Migrations/`. Creates `LiveChatConversations`, `LiveChatMessages`, foreign keys, indexes. If `Ticket.Channel` did not previously exist, adds a nullable `Channel` column with no backfill.
- **Rollback:** `dotnet ef migrations remove` before commit if regenerating. Post-deploy rollback: drop the two new tables; the nullable `Channel` column on `Ticket` can be left in place (nullable, non-breaking) or dropped in a follow-up migration.
- **Half-applied state:** migration wraps DDL in a single transaction. If it fails mid-way, EF rolls back — no orphan tables. Application will fail to start if `Ticket.Channel` is expected but missing; guard the write with a null-safe assignment.
- Permission seed additions in `DbSeeder.cs` are idempotent (upsert by permission name); safe to re-run.

## Verification Steps

1. **Backend builds:** `cd backend && dotnet build CustomerSupportCrm.slnx`.
2. **Backend migration applied:** `cd backend/src/CustomerSupportCrm.Api && dotnet ef database update`.
3. **Backend tests:** `cd backend && dotnet test`.
4. **Backend runs:** `cd backend/src/CustomerSupportCrm.Api && dotnet run` — hit `POST /api/live-chat/sessions` with curl; confirm 200 with `sessionToken`, `conversationId`, `ticketId`.
5. **SignalR handshake:** open two browser tabs, one as `/live-chat` (customer), one signed-in agent at `/live-chat/agent/conversations/{id}`. Send messages in both directions; confirm real-time delivery without refresh.
6. **Reconnect replay:** kill and restart the API; both clients auto-reconnect and existing messages remain visible.
7. **Frontend runs:** `cd frontend && pnpm install && pnpm dev`. Visit customer widget and agent workspace routes.
8. **Frontend tests:** `cd frontend && pnpm test`.
9. **Regression:** manually assign a Live Chat ticket through the existing ticket assignment UI (Story 12) — conversation moves to `Active` and agent receives `conversationStatusChanged`.
10. **Interaction history:** open the customer detail page; confirm the Live Chat interaction appears in the existing Customer Interaction History panel.
